text.arabic_uthmani: فَإِنْ عُثِرَ عَلَىٰٓ أَنَّهُمَا ٱسْتَحَقَّآ إِثْمًۭا فَـَٔاخَرَانِ يَقُومَانِ مَقَامَهُمَا مِنَ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱسْتَحَقَّ عَلَيْهِمُ ٱلْأَوْلَيَٰنِ فَيُقْسِمَانِ بِٱللَّهِ لَشَهَٰدَتُنَآ أَحَقُّ مِن شَهَٰدَتِهِمَا وَمَا ٱعْتَدَيْنَآ إِنَّآ إِذًۭا لَّمِنَ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ

words.gloss_range: consequence and sequence particle tying the ayah to the prior testimony procedure
words.prose: {{ar:فَ}} ({{tr:fa}}) opens 5:107 as a dependent consequence of the testimony procedure in 5:106. It makes the discovered-fraud scenario a remedy path: sequence and cause are both active, and the later discovery, replacement, source restriction, counter-oath, and self-imprecation all unfold from this bridge.

topics.headline: consequence opens the remedy clause
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah is not a fresh topic but the consequence pathway opened when the prior witness procedure fails.
topics.reason: The rows converge on the opening particle as a bridge from 5:106 and as the first segment of the ayah-wide conditional procedure.

words.gloss_range: conditional particle marking a possible but not presumed trigger
words.prose: {{ar:إِنْ}} ({{tr:in}}) keeps the fraud finding conditional. The replacement sequence is activated only if the condition is met, so the ayah protects the ordinary witness frame while still giving a precise route when that frame is breached.

topics.headline: fraud remains a contingency
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the law provides for possible witness fraud without making suspicion the default stance.
topics.reason: The conditional particle governs the protasis and the later apodosis, so the legal actions depend on a discovered contingency rather than an assumed offense.

words.gloss_range: completed passive discovery that triggers the legal remedy
words.root_gloss_range: stumbling, coming upon, and discovery; locally the passive discovery branch is selected
words.prose: {{ar:عُثِرَ}} ({{tr:ʿuthira}}) is a perfect passive: the finder is not named, and the completed discovery itself becomes the trigger. The root's stumbling or coming-upon image makes the breach feel like concealed evidence encountered underfoot, while the contrast with 18:21 keeps this local use marked as passive legal discovery rather than caused disclosure.

topics.headline: passive discovery surfaces a hidden breach
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the legal sequence waits for an established discovery, framed as hidden wrongdoing coming to the surface rather than suspicion hunting for a culprit.
topics.reason: The passive form, perfect aspect, root image, rarity rows, and 18:21 comparison all support a focused evidentiary trigger.

words.gloss_range: preposition routing passive discovery into a content clause
words.prose: {{ar:عَلَىٰٓ}} ({{tr:ʿalā}}) connects the passive discovery to the following content clause. Its ordinary upon-pressure remains useful: the fact is come upon in the legal surface, but grammar narrows it to what was discovered about the two witnesses.

topics.headline: upon governs the fact discovered
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that discovery is directed to the fact of guilt, not to a loose spatial object.
topics.reason: The preposition is attached to the passive discovery verb and governs the following content clause while retaining a spatial-to-abstract discovery idiom.

words.gloss_range: emphatic content introducer with dual pronoun pointing back to the prior pair
words.prose: {{ar:أَنَّهُمَا}} ({{tr:annahumā}}) supplies the discovered content and carries a definite dual pronoun. The ayah does not introduce a vague new pair; it routes the charge back to the two witnesses from 5:106 and lets the remedy depend on that carried referent.

topics.headline: dual pronoun fixes the accused witnesses
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the accusation is grammatically aimed at the same two witnesses already established in 5:106.
topics.reason: The content particle plus dual suffix identifies the prior two-person witness frame as the object of the discovered accusation.

words.gloss_range: Form X perfect dual: the two have made themselves liable for guilt
words.root_gloss_range: truth, right, binding reality, entitlement, and deservedness; local forms move from incurred liability to established right to comparative truth
words.prose: {{ar:ٱسْتَحَقَّآ}} ({{tr:istaḥaqqā}}) is perfect dual Form X, so the two witnesses have actively incurred the liability named by the next word. The root of right and binding reality is inverted here: what becomes established as due to them is guilt, and this first h-q-q occurrence starts the ayah's movement from earned guilt to restored right and then truer testimony.

topics.headline: right-root turns into earned guilt
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the moral reversal: language of right and due claim first appears as the witnesses making guilt due against themselves.
topics.reason: The rows agree that the Form X dual verb assigns self-incurred liability and begins the ayah’s repeated h-q-q reversal.

words.gloss_range: indefinite accusative guilt-liability object of the preceding verb
words.root_gloss_range: sin, guilt, burden, and delaying/holding back; locally an indefinite accusative liability object
words.prose: {{ar:إِثْمًۭا}} ({{tr:ithman}}) is the accusative object of the self-incurring verb and leaves the offense type indefinite. The root's burdening and holding-back associations fit the legal result: the first testimony is disabled by discovered guilt, and the word answers the self-imprecation formula of 5:106 in a new evidentiary setting.

topics.headline: guilt closes the condition without narrowing the offense type
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the condition ends on incurred guilt as an open liability category rather than a narrowly specified procedural detail.
topics.reason: The accusative syntax, indefiniteness, guilt semantics, and paired-ayah echo all make this the liability object that closes the protasis.

words.gloss_range: apodosis particle marking the result of the conditional discovery
words.prose: The second {{ar:فَ}} ({{tr:fa}}) marks the answer to the condition. It turns the established discovery into immediate procedural consequence: once guilt is found, another pair now stands in the failed pair's place.

topics.headline: result particle pivots into replacement
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the exact hinge where discovery becomes legal replacement.
topics.reason: The particle is the conditional apodosis marker and is locally attached to the replacement-witness clause.

words.gloss_range: indefinite nominative dual naming a replacement witness pair
words.root_gloss_range: otherness, lateness, and following after; locally a replacement pair after the first witnesses
words.prose: {{ar:آخَرَانِ}} ({{tr:ākharāni}}) names an indefinite nominative dual pair. Its otherness is procedural, not random: the pair follows after the first two, preserves the two-witness frame, and reverses the role of the same form used in 5:106.

topics.headline: another two become the remedy pair
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the remedy changes the persons but preserves the two-witness scale of the prior procedure.
topics.reason: The rows connect indefiniteness, dual morphology, replacement function, and the 5:106 recurrence into one procedural-substitution topic.

words.gloss_range: dual imperfect standing-in verb in a substitution construction
words.root_gloss_range: standing, rising, establishing, station, and role; locally legal standing and substitution are selected

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: standing-place or station occupied by the original two witnesses

words.prose: {{ar:يَقُومَانِ}} ({{tr:yaqūmāni}}) is dual imperfect, making the replacement action joint and procedurally available whenever the condition is met. With {{ar:مَقَامَهُمَا}} ({{tr:maqāmahumā}}), standing becomes assuming a role: the same q-w-m root covers both the act of standing and the station entered.

topics.headline: standing becomes role assumption
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the replacements do not merely appear; they jointly take up the legal role occupied by the first pair.
topics.reason: The verb’s dual imperfect form and its construction with the following maqām noun support a role-assumption reading rather than mere physical posture.

words.gloss_range: construct noun of place or station with dual suffix, functioning as the substitution target
words.root_gloss_range: standing, rising, establishing, station, and role; locally legal standing and substitution are selected
words.prose: {{ar:مَقَامَهُمَا}} ({{tr:maqāmahumā}}) packages q-w-m as a place or station and binds it by suffix to the original two witnesses. It can be heard locatively and as a cognate accusative, but locally both readings serve full substitution: the new pair occupies the failed pair's legal standing-place.

topics.headline: the failed pair’s station is transferred
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the replacements enter the exact legal station of the first witnesses, not merely a nearby speaking slot.
topics.reason: The construct suffix, noun-of-place pattern, accusative role, and adjacent q-w-m echo all converge on exact procedural replacement.

words.gloss_range: partitive source preposition selecting the group from which replacements come
words.prose: {{ar:مِنَ}} ({{tr:mina}}) restricts the source of the two replacements. It opens a partitive phrase that first locates the affected group and only afterward identifies the two most entitled members within it.

topics.headline: replacement source is restricted
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the replacement pair must come from the affected side, not from any arbitrary pool.
topics.reason: The rows identify the particle as partitive source marking, attached to the following relative phrase and entitlement noun.

words.gloss_range: plural relative pronoun introducing the clause that defines the affected group
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلَّذِينَ}} ({{tr:alladhīna}}) introduces the relative clause that defines the source group. Its plural form keeps the affected side broader than the two replacement speakers, so the counter-oath comes from within a harmed party rather than from isolated individuals.

topics.headline: relative clause identifies the aggrieved side
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the replacement source is defined by what was done against them, with a wider affected group behind the two speakers.
topics.reason: The plural relative pronoun heads the identifying clause for those against whom the right or claim fell.

words.gloss_range: Form X perfect in the relative clause, locally marking the right or claim established against the aggrieved side
words.root_gloss_range: truth, right, binding reality, entitlement, and deservedness; local forms move from incurred liability to established right to comparative truth

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: adversative prepositional phrase marking the affected plural group

words.prose: {{ar:ٱسْتَحَقَّ}} ({{tr:istaḥaqqa}}) repeats the Form X h-q-q root inside the source-defining clause. The accepted voice and subject pressures are real, but locally the phrase with {{ar:عَلَيْهِمُ}} ({{tr:ʿalayhimu}}) makes the reversal clear: the right or claim is established against the affected party, preparing the way for the entitled pair to answer.

topics.headline: right language reverses toward the aggrieved
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the second h-q-q occurrence turning the root from incurred guilt toward a claim established on behalf of the aggrieved party.
topics.reason: The canonical active surface, reported variant pressures, adversative preposition, and h-q-q recurrence are preserved, but the local syntax limits the topic to the aggrieved-party clause.

words.gloss_range: preposition plus plural suffix marking the affected party adversatively
words.prose: {{ar:عَلَيْهِمُ}} ({{tr:ʿalayhimu}}) routes the established claim back to the plural relative group. The upon-preposition functions adversatively here: the legal wrong has fallen against them, and the plural suffix keeps the harmed side wider than the dual replacement pair.

topics.headline: against them marks the harmed group
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the harm is directed against a plural affected side, while the later speakers are only two from within it.
topics.reason: The rows support an adversative prepositional relation whose plural pronoun resumes the relative group.

words.gloss_range: definite dual comparative identifying the two most entitled or nearest replacement speakers
words.root_gloss_range: nearness, adjacency, authority, and priority; locally entitlement by nearest/rightful relation is selected
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلْأَوْلَيَٰنِ}} ({{tr:al-awlayāni}}) closes the source phrase with a definite dual: the two nearest or most entitled ones. Variant and syntactic pressures sharpen the issue of agency and priority, while the local form keeps the payoff on relational entitlement within the aggrieved group.

topics.headline: the nearest entitled pair seals the source clause
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the replacement pair is selected by relational priority, not simply by availability.
topics.reason: The rows preserve qiraat and syntax issues, but local QAC and clause evidence narrow the word to the definite dual entitled-pair function.

words.gloss_range: sequential particle moving from standing replacement to oath action
words.prose: The third {{ar:فَ}} ({{tr:fa}}) moves the sequence from standing in place to swearing. Together with the earlier particles, it audibly segments the ayah into legal steps rather than letting the replacement and oath collapse into one undifferentiated action.

topics.headline: third consequence step moves into oath
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the procedural reset from taking the failed pair's place to performing the counter-oath.
topics.reason: The repeated particle is locally the sequencer into the oath clause and part of the ayah’s particle-driven architecture.

words.gloss_range: dual imperfect Form IV oath verb governing the oath-preposition phrase
words.root_gloss_range: dividing, allotting, and swearing; locally Form IV selects oath-taking while the division image still suits the legal sorting
words.prose: {{ar:يُقْسِمَانِ}} ({{tr:yuqsimāni}}) is a dual imperfect oath verb, assigning the speech-act jointly to the two replacements. The q-s-m field of swearing and division fits the legal sorting of truth from falsehood, and the same oath form answers 5:106 with reversed speakers.

topics.headline: the replacement pair jointly swear by God
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the remedy is not only replacement testimony but a reciprocal sworn act answering the oath frame of 5:106.
topics.reason: The verb’s dual form, Form IV oath sense, bāʾ complement, and 5:106 formula echo all support a reciprocal counter-oath topic.

words.gloss_range: oath preposition governing the divine name
words.prose: {{ar:بِ}} ({{tr:bi}}) is the oath bāʾ, the small preposition that supplies the sworn-by object. It binds the following divine name into the oath formula before the testimony claim begins.

topics.headline: oath bāʾ introduces the guarantor
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the oath is grammatically anchored before its claim is spoken.
topics.reason: All rows identify the particle as the oath preposition introducing the muqsam bihi.

words.gloss_range: proper divine name in genitive as the object of the oath preposition
words.root_gloss_range: the divine-name field with worship and deity; locally the proper divine name is the oath guarantor
words.prose: {{ar:ٱللَّهِ}} ({{tr:Allāhi}}) is genitive under the oath bāʾ and fixes the guarantor of the counter-oath. Derivational associations around deity, worship, or awe may color the name, but locally the proper divine name functions as the sworn-by authority, repeating the oath formula of 5:106.

topics.headline: the divine name anchors sworn accountability
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the counter-testimony is placed under divine accountability, not merely under social assertion.
topics.reason: The local grammar selects the proper divine name as oath object; broader derivational rows are kept as background, not as a replacement for that function.

words.gloss_range: emphatic oath-response lām attached to the testimony claim
words.prose: {{ar:لَ}} ({{tr:la}}) attaches emphasis to the testimony noun and opens the oath response. It makes the next phrase a sworn assertion, and it will be balanced by the later emphatic lām in the self-imprecation formula.

topics.headline: emphatic lām opens the oath response
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the exact marker where the oath turns into its asserted claim.
topics.reason: The rows identify this as the oath-response/emphatic lām fused to the direct speech claim.

words.gloss_range: verbal noun testimony with first-person plural possessive, subject of the sworn nominal clause
words.root_gloss_range: witnessing, presence, testimony, and attestation; locally legal testimony owned by competing parties is selected
words.prose: {{ar:شَهَٰدَتُنَآ}} ({{tr:shahādatunā}}) is a verbal noun with a first-person plural suffix, making witnessing a possessed legal claim: our testimony. It stages testimony against testimony in the nominal oath clause, while the sh-h-d field of presence and attestation carries the dispute toward 5:108, where testimony is restored to its proper face.

topics.headline: our testimony enters as a legal counter-claim
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices testimony becoming the contested object itself: the replacements own a counter-testimony that answers the first pair's claim.
topics.reason: The grammar, suffix, root semantics, local repetition with word 25, and 5:108 echo all converge on owned counter-testimony.

words.gloss_range: comparative predicate ranking the replacement testimony as more rightful or truer
words.root_gloss_range: truth, right, binding reality, entitlement, and deservedness; local forms move from incurred liability to established right to comparative truth
words.prose: {{ar:أَحَقُّ}} ({{tr:aḥaqqu}}) is the predicate of the sworn testimony claim. Its elative shape makes rightness comparative, not absolute in isolation: after h-q-q marked incurred guilt and established right, it now judges which testimony is more rightful.

topics.headline: comparative right judges the testimonies
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the h-q-q sequence landing on comparative truth: the same root that marked guilt now ranks the corrective testimony.
topics.reason: The rows support predicate grammar, comparative force, h-q-q root reprise, and the testimony-ranking function.

words.gloss_range: comparative preposition introducing the standard against which the testimony is ranked

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: comparative predicate ranking one testimony as more rightful

words.prose: {{ar:مِن}} ({{tr:min}}) is comparative here, not source-marking. It supplies the standard against which {{ar:أَحَقُّ}} ({{tr:aḥaqqu}}) works, so the counter-oath says the replacements' testimony is more rightful than the first pair's testimony.

topics.headline: than supplies the comparison standard
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the oath claims superiority over a specified testimony, not free-floating truthfulness.
topics.reason: The rows identify the particle as min al-tafdil and tie it to the following genitive testimony phrase.

words.gloss_range: genitive testimony noun with dual suffix completing the comparative frame
words.root_gloss_range: witnessing, presence, testimony, and attestation; locally legal testimony owned by competing parties is selected
words.prose: {{ar:شَهَٰدَتِهِمَا}} ({{tr:shahādatihimā}}) completes the comparative phrase and carries a dual suffix back to the original pair. The repeated sh-h-d noun with changed possession makes a direct contest: our testimony answers their testimony under the root of right.

topics.headline: their testimony is the precise target
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the counter-oath is aimed at the original two witnesses' own testimony, not at testimony in general.
topics.reason: The genitive construction, dual suffix, possessive contrast, and local root echo make this the exact rebutted testimony.

words.gloss_range: coordinating particle joining the positive testimony claim to the denial of transgression
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) keeps the oath from being a single expanded assertion. It coordinates the claim that the replacement testimony is more rightful with the separate denial that the speakers have not overstepped.

topics.headline: and coordinates claim with denial
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the oath has two coordinated contents: a positive claim and a defensive denial.
topics.reason: The rows converge on oath-content coordination and the structural separation of positive and negative clauses.

words.gloss_range: negation particle scoping over the perfect transgression verb
words.prose: {{ar:مَا}} ({{tr:mā}}) negates the following perfect verb. After the positive testimony claim, the oath becomes self-defensive: the speakers deny that their corrective counter-claim has already crossed the boundary into transgression.

topics.headline: negation turns the oath defensive
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the counter-witnesses defending their own legal boundary while asserting superior testimony.
topics.reason: The negation particle scopes over the perfect verb and balances the preceding positive assertion.

words.gloss_range: negated perfect Form VIII: we have not transgressed or overstepped
words.root_gloss_range: running beyond, crossing a limit, hostility, and transgression; locally denied legal overstepping is selected

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: negation particle scoping over the perfect transgression verb

words.prose: {{ar:ٱعْتَدَيْنَآ}} ({{tr:iʿtadaynā}}) is perfect Form VIII with the first-person plural speakers as subject, and it is negated by {{ar:مَا}} ({{tr:mā}}). The root image of crossing a limit remains apt: the oath denies completed legal overreach, tying the remedy to Surah 5's wider warnings about transgression, including 5:2 and 5:87.

topics.headline: the speakers deny overstepping the legal boundary
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the remedy is constrained: correcting false testimony must not itself become boundary-crossing.
topics.reason: The rows support the negated perfect form, boundary-crossing semantics, speaker accountability, and same-surah transgression thread.

words.gloss_range: emphatic particle plus first-person plural pronoun opening the self-imprecation clause
words.prose: {{ar:إِنَّآ}} ({{tr:innā}}) opens the emphatic self-imprecation with the same first-person plural speakers. It mirrors the closing structure of 5:106, but the final category changes, so the counter-oath accepts personal liability under a sharpened label.

topics.headline: indeed we opens personal liability
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the same speakers who assert and deny now place themselves under the consequence if the oath is false.
topics.reason: The rows identify the inna clause, repeated speaker identity, and formulaic mirror of 5:106.

words.gloss_range: consequence particle inside the self-imprecation formula
words.prose: {{ar:إِذًۭا}} ({{tr:idhan}}) supplies the in-that-case logic of the self-imprecation. It is the hinge from denied transgression to final classification, occupying the same consequence slot as the self-warning in 5:106.

topics.headline: then marks the false-oath consequence
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the denial carries conditional liability: if false, the speakers themselves fall under the closing verdict.
topics.reason: The rows support consequence meaning, closure movement, and the repeated 5:106 formula slot.

words.gloss_range: emphatic lām before the partitive predicate after inna
words.prose: The later {{ar:لَ}} ({{tr:la}}) is the slid emphatic lām before the predicate phrase. It reinforces the self-imprecation and mirrors the earlier lām: one asserts the testimony, the other asserts the consequence if the oath is false.

topics.headline: slid lām strengthens the final class verdict
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the final verdict being emphatically asserted, not merely appended.
topics.reason: The rows identify lām al-muzahlaqah and connect it to the closing class-membership formula.

words.gloss_range: partitive preposition marking membership in the wrongdoer class
words.prose: {{ar:مِنَ}} ({{tr:mina}}) is partitive in the closing formula. It makes the consequence membership: if the oath is false, the speakers are from among the wrongdoers.

topics.headline: from among makes the consequence class-membership
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that false counter-testimony would place the speakers among a recognized class, not only attach a single fault to them.
topics.reason: Both rows support partitive class membership in the final predicate.

words.gloss_range: definite plural active participle naming the class of wrongdoers
words.root_gloss_range: wrongdoing, injustice, misplacement, and darkness; locally the active-participle class of wrongdoers is selected
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ}} ({{tr:al-ẓālimīn}}) completes the predicate and seals the ayah with a definite plural active participle. The ẓ-l-m field of wrong, misplacement, and darkness is locally narrowed to legal-moral wrongdoing: false counter-testimony would put truth and right in the wrong place, escalating the mirrored closing from 5:106's guilt-bearers to wrongdoers.

topics.headline: wrongdoers seals the oath as misplacement of right
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the ayah closing not with generic guilt but with a class label for those who misplace right through false testimony.
topics.reason: The rows preserve the participial class label, root semantics, final-word closure, 5:106 contrast, and legal accountability echo while limiting darkness imagery to a coloring of misplacement.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The conditional opening at عثر and the paired clause آخران يقومان مقامهما.
baseline_models.mechanism: A concealed failure comes to light as the first pair's procedural stumble; the incurred sin disables their standing, so a matched pair occupies the same evidentiary office.

activation_trace.role: Emergence of a concealed matter makes the condition a forensic disclosure rather than a bare allegation.
The bodily stumble image supplies failure of footing and motivates loss of the first pair's procedural position.
Lagging behind the good casts the sin as failed or delayed fiduciary performance.
Exact standing-in-for another supplies transfer of the evidentiary office to the second pair.

changed_reading.before: Two disqualified witnesses are simply replaced.
changed_reading.after: Discovery initiates a designed reversal in which a hidden procedural fall vacates an office and a matched pair takes it over.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The three حق forms, the priority term الأوليان, and the comparative claim شهادتنا أحق.
baseline_models.mechanism: The repeated حق language moves through incurred obligation, a right borne against someone, and comparative priority. The second pair therefore voices the affected side's counterclaim, not merely a second version of the same report.

activation_trace.role: Fixed obligation links the first pair's incurred sin to a liability that the procedure must answer.
A specifically owned right makes the affected party's stake distributive rather than merely abstract truth.
Mutual assertion of right supplies the adversarial structure behind the two competing testimonies.
Priority and stronger entitlement identify the second speakers by their superior claim to take the procedural position.

changed_reading.before: The second testimony is only asserted to be factually truer.
changed_reading.after: The corrupted first claim generates a counter-entitlement, and the affected side asserts that its testimony has the stronger right to govern the outcome.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The oath, the two testimony nouns, and the denial وما اعتدينا followed by الظالمين.
baseline_models.mechanism: The oath places a knowledge-claim inside a protected boundary. The speakers deny both crossing that boundary and withholding a right, so the closing threat audits the scope and placement of testimony as well as its truthfulness.

activation_trace.role: A formal oath allocated among its bearers makes the claim solemn, shared, and procedurally accountable.
Declarative evidence grounded in knowledge defines what the oath is meant to warrant.
Crossing a limit turns the denial into a claim that the witnesses have not exceeded their evidentiary jurisdiction.
Withholding another's right names the concrete wrong that a false or overreaching testimony would commit.

changed_reading.before: The closing words are a generic assurance that the second pair did nothing wrong.
changed_reading.after: The second pair denies crossing the limits of what they may attest and trapping the claimants' right outside its proper holder.

context_deltas.mechanism: Earlier lawful and prohibited zones repeatedly define transgression as crossing a disclosed limit. That sequence sharpens the focus denial into a claim of procedural non-overreach.

activation_trace.role: Prohibition supplies one side of an explicit legal boundary.
Release from prohibition supplies the permitted side against which overreach can be measured.
Repeated boundary-crossing language directly links legal misclassification to transgression.
Transgression after a test adds the element of crossing a known limit after notice.
The focus denial applies that boundary logic to the rival testimony.

structural_cues: 5:87 places permission, self-made prohibition, and transgression in one sequence; 5:94 repeats transgression after a disclosed trial.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies repeated permitted/prohibited edges and post-notice crossing; I map that legal edge onto the evidentiary office in 5:107. The live alternative is that the focus phrase denotes generic moral wrongdoing without a jurisdictional nuance.

changed_reading.before: We did not transgress means only that we did not lie or behave badly.
changed_reading.after: We did not transgress also denies exceeding the right, role, or scope assigned to the counter-witnesses.

context_deltas.mechanism: The earlier oath rule distinguishes idle speech from deliberately bound oaths and commands their preservation; the later sequence allows oaths to follow and answer prior oaths. The focus oath is thus a binding but challengeable evidentiary instrument.

activation_trace.role: The oath sense identifies repeated sworn speech as a regulated legal act.
Binding and ratifying an undertaking supplies enforceability rather than mere emphasis.
Protecting a covenant makes oath-keeping an ongoing custody obligation.
Oaths following prior oaths show that sworn evidence can be procedurally answered rather than simply sealing the case.
The focus pair's formal oath is the local instrument placed inside that wider binding-and-answering system.

structural_cues: 5:89 contrasts unbound oath speech with deliberately bound oaths and provides repair; 5:108 explicitly sequences one set of oaths after another.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies binding, preservation, repair, and a second oath sequence; I infer that the focus oath carries a reversible procedural burden. It may instead function only as solemn corroboration, with no transfer of burden implied.

changed_reading.before: The second pair's oath is a one-way seal on their assertion.
changed_reading.after: The oath is a regulated and answerable instrument that shifts the burden after the first sworn account fails.

context_deltas.mechanism: The hunting-liability procedure uses judged equivalence and two just assessors to substitute an answering value for a violation. The witness procedure repeats the just pair, and the focus adds another pair standing in place, activating procedural compensation for corrupted evidence.

activation_trace.role: One thing standing for another supplies a compensatory substitution pattern.
Equivalence requires the substitute to answer the original loss rather than merely follow it.
Adjudication between people makes the equivalence a determined legal relation.
Equality and matching connect just assessors with an answering equivalent.
Joining one to one creates the paired unit that the focus procedure later duplicates.
Justice in judgment qualifies the original witness pair and links the two legal procedures structurally.
The focus pair's standing in place converts equivalent substitution into an evidentiary remedy.

structural_cues: 5:95 has two just persons determine an equivalent response to a violation; 5:106 has two just persons hold testimony; 5:107 answers their failure with another pair.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies two-person adjudication, equivalence, and explicit substitution; I transfer that compensatory logic from material liability to evidentiary repair. The alternative is that the shared pair formula is formal parallelism without a common mechanism.

changed_reading.before: The second pair merely supersedes untrustworthy speakers.
changed_reading.after: The counter-pair functions as an answering equivalent that restores procedural balance after the first pair has distorted a right.

context_deltas.mechanism: The context moves from what is made visible or concealed, through the ban on concealing testimony, to testimony delivered on its proper face and the possibility of rejecting prior oaths. This turns the focus discovery into an error-correcting disclosure path.

activation_trace.role: Appearance and emergence establish the visible pole of the disclosure mechanism.
Concealment supplies the hidden state from which evidence must be recovered.
The witnesses' explicit denial of concealment localizes that hidden-visible contrast inside the testimony procedure.
The correct aspect of a matter gives recovered testimony its proper orientation.
Rejecting what is false or defective supplies the corrective action applied to the prior oath.
A concealed trace disturbed into visibility gives the focus discovery a material evidentiary texture.
A sign that bears witness lets the surfaced trace support correction of the human account.

structural_cues: 5:99 pairs disclosure with concealment; 5:106 forbids concealed testimony; 5:108 joins proper-facing testimony to rejection of prior oaths.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies hidden and visible poles, a non-concealment pledge, proper orientation, and rejection; I connect them as a disclosure-to-correction pipeline. A live alternative is that proper face means only accurate verbal performance, not recovery of hidden evidence.

changed_reading.before: A chance discovery simply triggers a fresh witness pair.
changed_reading.after: A concealed trace is surfaced, oriented into proper testimony, and used to reject or correct the defective sworn account.

context_deltas.mechanism: The later interrogation separates finite witnesses from knowledge of the hidden, then explicitly limits witnesshood to the duration of presence and transfers watching after removal. The focus claim of being more حق becomes comparative epistemic standing, not possession of total truth.

activation_trace.role: Knowledge as disclosure distinguishes what finite respondents can know from what the knower of hidden things knows.
What is screened from sight marks the epistemic region unavailable to ordinary witnesses.
Witnesshood grounded in presence supplies the condition under which testimony has jurisdiction.
Duration bounds that witnessing presence in time.
Taking the person away terminates the first witness's direct observational office.
Ongoing observation after the transfer supplies a distinct and superior watching office.
Truth matching reality remains the focus standard, while the comparative form ranks access to it.

structural_cues: 5:109 has questioned messengers disclaim knowledge before the knower of hidden things; 5:117 states a witness-duration clause and then transfers watching after removal.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies finite knowledge, hidden knowledge, presence-bounded witnesshood, and transferred watching; I map that epistemic hierarchy onto the local comparison of testimonies. The alternative is that local witnesses may know through custody or transmission without direct presence.

changed_reading.before: Our testimony is more حق asserts unrestricted possession of the truth.
changed_reading.after: Our testimony has the stronger warrant within a bounded field of presence, access, and procedural standing.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it carries a material pack-load image into adjudication. It remains anchored in the matched pair standing in place and in the packet's repeated just pairs; downstream prose should present it only as a structural analogy for counterweight, not as the lexical meaning of the verse.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The matched substitution in آخران يقومان مقامهما.

activation_trace.role: Standing exactly where another stood supplies the replacement side of the balancing mechanism.
A load balancing another load materializes the answering equivalent as a counterweight.
Applying the same balance image to the first witness pair lets the second pair occupy the opposite evidentiary side.
One joined to one fixes the stable paired unit needed for a matched counterload.

changed_reading.before: The two later witnesses only replace the first two sequentially.
changed_reading.after: The second pair can be carried as an exploratory counterload that rebalances the evidentiary weight borne by the first pair.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it combines dust-trace, witnessing-sign, and penetrating-thrust branches into a forensic material analogy. It remains anchored in عثر, شهادة, and أحق within the focus ayah; downstream prose should qualify it as an exploratory image of evidentiary force, not claim that nonhuman trace evidence is the verse's settled referent.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The sequence from عثر to the comparative شهادتنا أحق.

activation_trace.role: A hidden trace stirred into visibility supplies evidence independent of the rival speakers' assertions.
A mark that testifies allows the discovered trace to function as corroborating sign.
A straight thrust that penetrates supplies the exploratory image of evidence reaching through a defective surface account.

changed_reading.before: Only one human statement defeats another human statement.
changed_reading.after: A surfaced trace may be carried as a witnessing sign whose evidentiary force penetrates the first pair's account.

strongest_changes: The focus becomes an error-correcting reversal: concealed failure is surfaced, the first pair's office is vacated, and a matched counterpair restores the affected side's claim.
The oath is a bound but answerable evidentiary instrument rather than a one-way seal.
More rightful testimony is comparative and jurisdiction-bounded by presence and access rather than a claim to omniscience.
summary.what_was_special: Repeated two-person adjudication, equivalent substitution, returned oaths, and the later transfer from finite witness to continuing watcher made the focus read as a compact protocol for correcting corrupted testimony. Material branches preserved distinct counterload and trace-evidence outliers.
remaining_uncertainties: The syntactic direction of the affected group and the priority term remains open, so the exact holder of the counter-entitlement is not fully resolved.
The transfer from compensatory equivalence to evidentiary counterweight may be a structural analogy rather than a shared legal mechanism.
Presence-bounded witnesshood may illuminate comparative warrant without strictly governing the local witnesses' competence.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **Discovered breach triggers procedural substitution.** `ع ث ر B001` is uncovering a hidden matter, `ق و م B007` standing in another's place, and `و ل ي B008` superior right. I infer that procedure contains its own corrective reversal: nearer claimants replace compromised witnesses at the same station.
2. **Competing testimony is ranked by due claim, not force.** `ح ق ق B002` is deserved obligation and `B004` contesting claims. Repetition around both sides makes the issue comparative right. I infer that the second oath does not erase contest but reanchors it in the injured claimants' standing.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: Later ayah 5:120 made the fixed ayah's local distinctions newly visible as bounded operations within a single encompassing dominion, rather than as an isolated rule or episode.

reader_a.activated_readings_md: 1. **Discovery triggers procedural substitution rather than collapse of testimony.** Fixed **ع ث ر / B001** (“discovering or being shown a hidden matter”) activates the correction, and fixed **ق و م / B007** (“substitution and standing in another’s place”) is doubled in *yaqūmāni maqāmahumā*. 5:106 contained the first witnesses; 5:108 explains that the possibility of reversed oaths promotes truthful delivery. I infer that the system preserves the testimonial office while replacing corrupted occupants with claimants nearer the harmed right. Exposure therefore repairs the channel instead of merely discrediting it.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 5:108 explicitly supplied the procedure’s prospective purpose, showing that replacement repairs present corruption by changing the first witnesses’ incentives in advance.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_semantic_invariant: A truthful deposition is protected by procedures that confine, test, expose, and replace compromised witnesses.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_surprising_reach: Reliability is produced through a repairable social mechanism rather than assumed as a fixed property of the first witnesses.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: Hidden Fault Triggers a Substitute Witness
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: Discovery of culpability activates closer claimants, who stand in the first witnesses’ place and return the oath against them.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: The procedure is self-correcting. Once concealed fault reaches the surface, positional substitution and a reversed oath re-route authority toward those with the stronger claim.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi, gizli ya da önceden bilinmeyen bir durumu öğrenme ile bir başkasının o durumu öğrenmesini sağlama yönlerini açıkça ayırır. Aramadan ve beklenmedik biçimde öğrenme özelliği, temel öğrenme yönünün önemli bir sınırıdır.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Bu dal tökezleme, toz veya iz bildirmez; bilinmeyen bir duruma erişme ve eriştirme ile sınırlıdır.

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım, bir yapıda aramadan öğrenme yönünü, ettirgen yapıda ise başkasına bilgi kazandırma yönünü ayrı tutar.

concept_map.definition: Gizli ya da önceden bilinmeyen bir durumu, özellikle onu aramadan, öğrenip fark etmek veya bir başkasının bu durumu öğrenmesini sağlamaktır.

facets.statement: Gizli ya da önceden bilinmeyen bir durumu, kimi zaman aramadan ve beklenmedik biçimde öğrenip fark etme.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar, bilinmeyen bir durumu öğrenme ile birini o durumdan haberdar etme ayrımında birleşir. Bazı anlatımlarda öğrenmenin özellikle arama olmadan gerçekleştiği belirtilir.

lexicalization_scope.note: Toz ve iz bildiren biçimler ayrı korunur; iz bulunmadığını bildiren yapı yalnız kendi olumsuz bağlamında yorumlanır.

Ekin için kazılan su yolu aynı tanıklıkta yer alsa da ekinin doğal su kaynağıyla beslenmesini tanımlayan çekirdeğin zorunlu parçası değil, suyu ona yönelten ilişkili araçtır.

identity_judgment.boundary_note: Dal, bir şeyin gerçekliğe uygun ve doğru oluşunu anlatır; çekişme, yükümlülük ve kişiye ait pay bu dalın dışında kalır.

concept_map.definition: Bir düşüncenin, sözün ya da durumun gerçekten var olana uygun düşmesi ve bu nedenle yanlışın karşısında doğru, sağlam ve kesin sayılmasıdır. Söz bakımından ayrıca eğretilemenin karşısındaki gerçek anlamı kapsar.

facets.statement: Gerçekte var olana uygun düşen şey doğru ve sağlamdır.
Bir konuyu araştırıp doğruluğundan kesin biçimde emin olma bu çekirdeğin bilgi alanındaki uzantısıdır.
Bir sözün eğretileme olmadan ilk konulduğu anlamda kullanılması, dil alanındaki özel görünümüdür.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Toplu tanıklık, yanlışın karşısındaki doğruluğu gerçekliğe uygunlukla açıklar; kesin olarak öğrenmeyi ve sözün eğretilemesiz gerçek anlamını da aynı anlam alanına bağlar.

concept_gloss.applicability: Bir düşüncenin, sözün veya durumun gerçekten var olana uygun ve yanlışın karşıtı olduğunu bütün çekirdeğiyle anlatmak için kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Gerçekliğe uygunluk, doğruluk ve kesinlik öğelerinin tümünü korur.

error_profile.loses: Kesin bilgi ile gerçek anlam kullanımını tek başına belirtmez.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Bir sözün eğretileme değil, ilk ve doğrudan anlamında kullanıldığını belirtirken uygundur.

error_profile.preserves: Dilsel kullanımın eğretilemesiz ve yerli yerinde oluşunu korur.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi bir şeyin gerekli ve bağlayıcı hale gelmesini, bir kişinin ona layık ya da onunla yükümlü olmasını, ayrıca gerekli kılma ve hak etme işlemlerini birlikte verir. Dal çerçevesi bu ilişkileri doğru toplar.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Çekirdek, bir işin bağlayıcı biçimde gerekli olması veya bir sonucun kişiye düşmesidir; yalnızca doğru olma ya da özel mülkiyet payı değildir.
